items.title: Denny Zeitlin interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: I tend to think of people like Charlie Parker, Bud Powell, Miles Davis, John Coltrane, George Russell, Ornette Coleman, people like that.

ctx.x: Wow. Well said. I had a question and you just made me forget it. That was so interesting what you were saying. Do you have people that, in your opinion, would be considered to be musical geniuses? I think that personally speaking the word genius is bandied about an awful lot. And I’m wondering, in the people that you enjoy listening to over the years, have there been a couple that you would consider to be geniuses?

I agree with you that the word is so highly charged and it would be so difficult to define. I mean I do think, when I think of the real incredible innovators and trailblazers in our music I tend to think of people like Charlie Parker, Bud Powell, Miles Davis, John Coltrane, George Russell, Ornette Coleman, people like that. I think — Wayne Shorter is another huge giant in my view in terms of a kind of unique contribution to the music over a long period of time. I’m sure I’m leaving out people that I love. Because…
Okay. If I was to look — I’m assuming maybe you have a shelf of CDs or LPs.
